response.message:
I've drawn the full flow on Google Cloud: synthetic device events go into Pub/Sub, Dataflow validates and de-duplicates them, Vertex AI scores them, results land in BigQuery and Cloud Monitoring alerts an operator. Nothing is deployed or tested, no region is chosen, and the first local test can only check the pipeline logic with a stand-in model, which tells us nothing about real anomaly-detection quality.

How long after an event's own timestamp should we still accept it, for example within 10 minutes, and what should happen to anything later than that: reject it, store it separately, or rescore it?

proposal.title: Google Cloud sensor anomaly pipeline (first concrete sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic sensor events → Pub/Sub ingestion (retained for replay) → Dataflow validation, dedup and event-time windowing → Vertex AI inference → BigQuery results → Cloud Monitoring operator alert. Rejects go to a Pub/Sub dead-letter topic; raw events are archived in Cloud Storage for replay. Assumptions: region not chosen; model type, late-data policy and alert thresholds still open; service interoperability and quotas not verified; no native Terraform generator exists for this workload, so engineering is required.

data.label: Synthetic sensor simulator
data.description: Existing test caller outside provisioning scope. Emits events with device_id, event_id, event timestamp, value and unit, including duplicates, late, out-of-order, unknown-device and bad-unit cases.

data.label: Telemetry ingest topic
data.description: Durable buffer with message retention and seek-to-timestamp for replay after disconnection. Ordering key = device_id. Publisher uses a dedicated service account.

data.label: Raw event archive
data.description: Unmodified raw events written by Dataflow for longer-term replay and audit, beyond Pub/Sub retention.

data.label: Device registry
data.description: Known devices and their allowed units. Dataflow checks every event against it; unknown devices are rejected.

data.label: Validation and windowing pipeline
data.description: Apache Beam streaming job: validates the schema, device and unit; removes duplicates by event_id; uses event-time windows with an explicit allowed-lateness policy (still open); builds feature windows while keeping device_id, timestamps and units unchanged; calls the model.

data.label: Rejected events topic
data.description: Dead-letter topic for unknown devices, invalid units and events past the lateness limit, each with a rejection reason.

data.label: Anomaly model endpoint
data.description: Serves the anomaly model and returns a score, the evidence features and the model version. In local tests this is a scripted mock, not a validated model.

data.label: Model registry
data.description: Versioned anomaly models; the deployed version is stamped on every result.

data.label: Anomaly results
data.description: One row per device window, written idempotently using a deterministic key: device_id, window, score, evidence, model_version and original units and timestamps.

data.label: Operator alerting
data.description: Alert policy on anomaly results and pipeline health (backlog, dead-letter rate).

data.label: Operator
data.description: Person who receives anomaly alerts. Notification channel still to be chosen.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents bad data from producing false anomalies.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Reject unknown device and invalid units.
requirementDrafts.statement: Reject events from unknown devices or with invalid units, sending each to a dead-letter topic with the reason.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Pub/Sub can deliver a message more than once, so without this we get double alerts.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Duplicate events produce one result.
requirementDrafts.statement: Duplicate events must produce exactly one result.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without a policy, results depend on arrival order.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Late and out-of-order telemetry follows an explicit policy.
requirementDrafts.statement: Late and out-of-order telemetry follows an explicit event-time lateness policy (value still open).

requirementDrafts.rationale: Makes recovery safe after an outage.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: Disconnected input recovers by replay.
requirementDrafts.statement: Recover from disconnected input by replaying retained or archived events without creating duplicate results.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Lets operators trust and audit each alert.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: Anomaly output names evidence and model version; preserve device identity, timestamps and units.
requirementDrafts.statement: Each anomaly result names its evidence and the model version, and keeps the original device_id, timestamps and units.

response.message: No runtime checks ran, so nothing here is validated yet. The emulation stopped before testing because none of our Google Cloud parts (Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Firestore, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Vertex AI) has a supported code template yet. Changing the diagram can't fix that, so I've left it as it is; the fix is product engineering work, and the first piece would be a native Pub/Sub and Dataflow template that runs the "unknown device gets rejected" case end to end. While that's built, let's settle the decision that is ours to make: how long after an event's own timestamp should we still accept it, for example 10 minutes, and should anything later be rejected, stored separately or rescored?
